title: Uruguay at the World Cup
description: The two-time champions from South America — winners in 1930 and 1950. How well do you know La Celeste?

questions.q: Uruguay won the first ever World Cup in 1930. In which city was it held?
questions.explain: Montevideo, Uruguay hosted the first World Cup in 1930. Uruguay beat Argentina 4–2 in the final at the Estadio Centenario, watched by a crowd of around 93,000.

questions.q: Uruguay won their second World Cup in 1950 with a legendary victory. What is the name given to that match?
questions.explain: The Maracanazo refers to Uruguay's 2–1 win over Brazil in the 1950 deciding match at the Maracanã. A crowd of almost 200,000 Brazilians expected a home win — the result devastated a nation.

questions.q: Uruguay's 1930 World Cup final win over Argentina was played at which famous stadium?
questions.explain: The Estadio Centenario in Montevideo — built specifically for the 1930 World Cup — hosted the final. The stadium, named to mark Uruguay's centenary of independence, holds a UNESCO World Heritage designation.

questions.q: At the 2010 World Cup, Luis Suárez deliberately handled a goal-bound shot on the line to deny Ghana in extra time. What happened next?
options: Suárez was allowed to stay on — Ghana missed the penalty and Uruguay went through
Suárez was given a red card, Ghana scored the penalty, Ghana went through
Uruguay conceded a penalty but also kept 11 men on the pitch
questions.explain: Suárez was sent off for the handball but Asamoah Gyan struck the resulting penalty against the crossbar. Uruguay won the shootout and advanced. Suárez called himself 'the hero' — Ghana were heartbroken.

questions.q: Who won the Golden Ball (best player) at the 2010 World Cup while playing for Uruguay?
questions.explain: Diego Forlán won the Golden Ball in 2010 after a superb individual tournament, including two stunning long-range goals. He was playing for Atlético Madrid at the time.

questions.q: Edinson Cavani scored twice as Uruguay beat Portugal in the 2018 World Cup round of 16. What was the final score?
questions.explain: Cavani scored a brace — including a stunning long-range volley — to eliminate Cristiano Ronaldo's Portugal 2–1. Ronaldo was left carrying an injured Cavani off the pitch in a touching gesture.

questions.q: Óscar Tabárez guided Uruguay across multiple World Cups in one of the longest tenures in international football. Roughly how many years did he manage the team?
questions.explain: Tabárez managed Uruguay from 2006 to 2021 — about 15 years — overseeing the team at four World Cups (2006, 2010, 2014, 2018) and winning the 2011 Copa América.

questions.q: Uruguay reached the semi-finals at the 2010 World Cup. Which European team knocked them out?
questions.explain: The Netherlands beat Uruguay 3–2 in the semi-final, with goals from Robben, Sneijder and Robben. Uruguay lost the third-place match to Germany 3–2.

questions.q: Uruguay's national team shirt is light blue. What is their traditional nickname?
questions.explain: La Celeste — 'the sky-blue' — is Uruguay's most common nickname, taken from the colour of their famous shirt. Los Charrúas (after the indigenous people of Uruguay) is also used.

questions.q: How many times has Uruguay won the Copa América?
questions.explain: Uruguay have won the Copa América 15 times — more than any other nation — though Argentina and Brazil have dominated in recent decades. Their last Copa América win was in 2011.
